newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ADAM HOLLIOAKE CONTINUES TO SHINE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ADAM HOLLIOAKE CONTINUES TO SHINE.

text.p: England hero Adam Hollioake continued his magical week on Tuesday by leading Surrey to the semi-finals of the Benson and Hedges Cup as they brushed aside Essex by six wickets.
The Surrey skipper, named man of the series in the Texaco Trophy series whitewash against Australia, took two wickets, held a catch and claimed a run out to wrap up the Essex innings for 214.
He could then relax as fellow England star Graham Thorpe scored 73 to guide his side to 215 for four with over seven overs left.

Joining Surrey in the semi-finals were last year's beaten finalists Northamptonshire, who were lifted to a seven-wicket win over Yorkshire at Headingley by David Capel's five wickets and half-century.

Matthew Walker's century steered Kent to a four-wicket verdict with just three balls to spare against Warwickshire in a high-scoring contest at Canterbury, while county champions Leicestershire booked their place with a 20-run victory over Somerset at Grace Road.

Hollioake's side cantered home with 45 balls to spare, pinch-hitter and younger brother Ben Hollioake blasting 17 from nine balls to follow his own England heroics by helping take the club to their eighth Benson and Hedges semi-final and first since 1994.
When opener Alistair Brown clubbed, there was little doubt Surrey would reach their target.
Former test player Capel produced a stunning all-round display to ease Northamptonshire through with four overs to spare as they reached 254 for three in response to Yorkshire's 253 for nine.

Capel, who played his last Test eight years ago, claimed career-best bowling figures in the competition of five for 51 before devastating Yorkshire's attack with 67 off 59 balls to give Northants the platform for a comfortable triumph.

Neil Smith scored 125 for Warwickshire but his efforts proved in vain as fellow opener Walker's 117, the left-hander's maiden limited-overs century, guided Kent to 306 for six in reply to the visitors' 304 for eight.
Warwickshire were hampered by an injury to pace ace Allan Donald, who went off with a side strain after bowling only two overs.
Leicestershire overcame a disastrous start thanks to three wickets apiece by pace duo David Millns and Alan Mullally.
Somerset were chasing what appeared a modest 198 target but Millns and Mullally ripped out the first five Somerset wickets for only 57 runs as they were dismissed for 177 with 13 deliveries unused.
Leicestershire had earlier recovered from 14 for three thanks to a 102-run stand between skipper James Whitaker (51) and Ben Smith (61).
